## Context / Problem

Epic 62dc's criterion 5 is undelivered: plan review never tells a reviewer that the plan under review overlaps work another ticket describes. Each plan is read in isolation, so two tickets planning one change both pass. Create-time surfacing matches a title plus a short description; plan review runs later against a full plan, far more material. One index serves both.

## Approach

**Reuse the index; add no second retrieval path.** The sibling story builds a lexical FTS5 index under `.rebar/cache/similar-tickets/`, caught up in the read phase, no daemon. Its whole public surface is `find_similar` (`src/rebar/similar/__init__.py:46-54`, stated at `:8`), taking query text via `text=` (`:51`, resolved at `:73`) plus `exclude_id=` to drop self-hits (`:52`), so plan material needs no new retrieval module. With the optional embedding tier configured it ranks through that tier, otherwise lexically (`:79-82`): no model provider is required.

**The one gap: failure distinguishability.** Every failure returns `[]`, per "Never raises" (`:55`), so a caller cannot tell an absent index from a failed catch-up from an empty match.

**Diagnostic contract.** `find_similar` gains one keyword-only parameter `diagnostics: dict | None = None`; given a dict it records a `status` plus a human `detail`. The set is closed, being one value per branch: `index-absent` `:63`, `catch-up-failed` `:66-71`, `retrieval-error` at the outer handler `:84`, else `ok` (`:80` embedding, `:82` lexical). An embedding-provider failure is NOT a status: `embedding.rank` returns `None` for every cause it cannot serve -- unconfigured, backend absent, provider failing, coverage incomplete (`:76-79`) -- with `:82` then serving lexical results, so that path is `ok`. Return type, "Never raises", every existing call stay unchanged: the signal travels through the dict. The only `src/` consumer is `recent_creates.py:196` (imported `:27`), which passes no `diagnostics`.

**Recording channel: coverage, written in place.** `run_pass1` takes `coverage` as a mutable dict (`pass1.py:238`), assigning diagnostic keys into it directly -- `coverage["isf"]` `:473`, `coverage["recall_candidates"]` `:521`; `coverage["overlap"]` is written the same way. `coverage_extra` is not the seam: it belongs to `indeterminate_verdict` (`claimability.py:132`), reached only on the LLM-skipping early returns the overlap path never takes.

**Ride the existing Pass-1 extra-context seam.** A Pass-1 finder unit already accepts store-derived `extra_context` (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/checkpoints.py:54`), its identity binding that context by `context_digest`, a sha256 over the injected text (`:61-63`, carried at `:70`), under the discovery contract `plan_review_findings` (`passes.py:122`). That text is built by `_chunk_extra_context` (`pass1.py:215`), whose single call site `:326` feeds `_discovery_unit_plan` `:331` plus `checkpoint_identity` `:339`, so injection lands in `pass1.py`. The seam is live: `:219-222` already injects G5 context. Appending candidates there rather than adding a pass leaves checkpoint identity plus caching unchanged: a changed candidate set yields a different `context_digest`.

**Zero marginal LLM cost: the existing Pass-1 unit does the judging.** Candidates ride a chunk already being sent, so overlap judging adds no LLM call; lexical retrieval is not one either. The cap is therefore on candidates, not calls. It is 5, the default `RESULT_LIMIT` (`similar/lexical.py:39`): ADR 0122 makes k=5 load-bearing -- at k=10 the vector tier's advantage vanishes into noise -- so overlap keeps that operating point rather than forcing a `--paired` re-run.

**On demand, not on every review.** The switch is one keyword-only parameter `overlap: bool = False` on `review_plan` (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py:199`), threaded exactly as `probe_criteria` is, because `review_plan` assembles no batch request. The chain: `review_plan` -> `gate_dispatch.produce_plan_review_verdict` (`workflow/gate_dispatch.py:64`, called at `__init__.py:473`) -> `run_workflow` inputs (`:183`) -> a new `overlap:` input in `workflow/gates/plan-review.yaml` (`:24` declares `probe_criteria`) wired into the finders batch `with:` (`:54`, `:66`) -> `req.with_inputs` -> `ProductionBatchRunner.run` (`production_batch_runner.py:123`) -> `run_pass1` (`pass1.py:232`) -> `_chunk_extra_context`. Always threaded, `False` = off, so `${{ inputs.overlap }}` always resolves.

**The injected block's decision rule is enforced by posture, not by prompt.** Mirroring `decomposition_state_block` (`det_lint.py:46`), `overlap.py` emits a `## POSSIBLE OVERLAP (from store)` heading, a directive to judge whether this plan does work a listed ticket already describes, then one `alias -- title (status)` line per candidate, the shape at `:66-70`. "Never block" is no prompt wish: the decide pass partitions on each finding's `decision` (`orchestrator.py:294-301`), keyed to its criterion's `default_posture` (`det_invariants.py:85`). The finding is therefore attributed to a new `project.plan-overlap` entry in `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` carrying `default_posture: "advisory"` -- the shape `project.symbol-reference-completeness` already has -- which the decide pass can never place in `blocking`.

**Degradation.** On any non-`ok` status the candidate list is empty, no overlap finding is emitted, the review proceeding to its normal verdict.

**The injection site has little headroom, so the work is extracted.** `pass1.py` is 658 lines against the 800 cap, so overlap retrieval plus its diagnostic live in a new `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/overlap.py`; `_chunk_extra_context` gains only the call.

Any ratcheted mechanism added carries a `# mechanism-ok:` marker naming this ticket at its definition site.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] With `overlap=True`, reviewing a ticket whose plan restates an existing ticket's plan emits an advisory overlap finding naming that ticket. Checked by: a seeded-store test asserting the finding names that id.
- [ ] At most 5 candidates are injected into the Pass-1 extra context. Checked by: a test on a store seeded with over 5 matches asserting exactly 5 injected.
- [ ] With `overlap=True`, the LLM call count equals that of the same review with `overlap=False`. Checked by: a test comparing both counts.
- [ ] The off switch is total, one test per case: with `overlap=False` no overlap finding is emitted; the run's checkpoint identity stays byte-identical to the same review before this change.
- [ ] An overlap finding can never turn a verdict from pass to block, one test per case: it is attributed to a criterion whose routing `default_posture` is `advisory`; the decide pass places it in `advisory`; a passing plan's verdict is unchanged with one present.
- [ ] `find_similar` called without `diagnostics` returns exactly what it did before this change. Checked by: a test asserting the `recent_creates.py:196` call yields an unchanged result.
- [ ] With no model provider configured, overlap retrieval still returns lexical-tier candidates. Checked by: a test with provider credentials cleared asserting a non-empty candidate set.
- [ ] On each non-`ok` status (`index-absent`, `catch-up-failed`, `retrieval-error`) the verdict equals that of the same review with `overlap=False`. Checked by: one test per status comparing both verdicts.
- [ ] `coverage["overlap"]["status"]` records `index-absent` when the index is absent, `catch-up-failed` when catch-up raises, `retrieval-error` when retrieval raises. Checked by: one test per status asserting that value, with the overlap finding set empty.
- [ ] Every module added or modified under `src/rebar/` is at most 800 lines. Checked by: the module-size gate.
- [ ] `python scripts/check_mechanism_delta.py --check` exits 0. Checked by: running it.
- [ ] `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check` exits 0. Checked by: running it.
